BiblicalUsage: Baalah as a common word means a mistress — the woman who owns or rules. The mistress of the house at Zarephath, whose son Elijah raised, is called the baalah of the house; the witch of Endor is a mistress of a familiar spirit; and Nineveh is called the mistress of witchcrafts, that selleth nations through her whoredoms. One word, three very different mistresses.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the contrast is the whole lesson: the widow of Zarephath was a mistress who trusted the prophet, and Nineveh was a mistress who sold nations. The title is neutral; the heart is not.
